paper.title_en: The Clay & Silicon Putty Model — Version 4.0: A Coarse-Grained Structure-Activated Interacting Vacuum Cosmology
paper.abstract_en:
The Clay & Silicon Putty Model — Version 4.0 presents a minimal, coarse-grained interacting-vacuum cosmology designed to test whether late-time cosmic expansion can be modified without violating independent constraints on structure growth.

The Level-I framework introduces no new particle species, mediator, fifth force, or modified gravitational-wave propagation speed. Instead, it treats the dark matter-like sector and a vacuum-like negative-pressure sector as interacting stress–energy components within general relativity. Their background energy-transfer rate is modulated by a pre-specified structure-formation activation kernel and controlled by a single continuous interaction parameter, (\xi).

The activation kernel is explicitly treated as a phenomenological, coarse-grained closure rather than a derived local microscopic field. The model therefore makes no claim of a complete fundamental theory.

Its principal test is whether any improvement in low-redshift expansion-history fits remains consistent with CMB lensing, redshift-space distortions, (f\sigma_8), (S_8), weak gravitational lensing, matter clustering, supernovae, and DESI measurements. The paper defines the background evolution, covariant interaction prescription, linear perturbation framework, ΛCDM null limit, assumptions, observational tests, falsification criteria, and the numerical program required for implementation in an Einstein–Boltzmann solver.
